# Chapter Six: The Traveling Priest

Traveling Priest

Nero had noticed the change almost immediately after leaving the old barn and heading north. Soldiers had taken to patrolling all of the heavier trafficked marketing routes and the usual traffic of farmers and carts bound for market were no more. “Are they still there” the old man whispered Nero could smell the old meat of breakfast barely vield by the stick of mint he now chewed. “Yes” he simply whispered back as the two men hit within the underbrush near the edge of the farmers trail leading to the village about four miles up the road.

“What are they doing?” he whispered and Nero shot him an annoyed look he knew the old man could see the same thing he did, Soldiers standing in the road talking, he didn’t know why he thought Nero might have some extra insight into there motivations but appearent he did “Standing in the road and talking” he whispered back. He caught the old man rolling his eyes out of his peripheral vision. “I can see that, I mean what are they talking about” he said, and Nero half turned towards the old man, having had just about enough of the conversation. “I don’t know, why don’t you go ask them” he said and then turned back to watching the soldiers.

“Oh, a joke” he said and chuckled lightly. Nero just shook his head, most of the time, Gil Haverdash was a decent traveling companion until times like this he reflected. The two continued to watch the soldiers for what seemed like forever, finally, mercifully thought Nero still fielding the obvious questions from Gil. The soldiers turned and continued down the road towards the village, which he assumed meant they were continuing their patrol, they would have to be mindful of them returning as they walked, he thought coming out of the brush as they disappeared around the bend.

“Took them long enough” Gill said, and Nero could hear the annoyance in the man’s voice. Nodding he motioned for Gill to follow and began walking towards the village. “What are you doing?” he asked concerned. Nero turned to look at the old man “Walking North, as he said we were going to” he simply stated. Gil shook his head as if he didn’t quite believe what the Messenger was saying. “But not the same way the soldiers went my friend, I suggest we stick to the brush and walk in parralell to the road, thus not allowing ourselves to become unwary volunteers in a trap” he finished and Nero thought about it for a moment, that was actually sage advice he thought and deflating a little, Gil was right, he should listen to the other man and not allow his annoyance or pride get in the way. “Very well, I will follow you my friend” he said motioning for Gil to take the lead.

With a pat on Nero’s back Gil passed him and the Messenger followed Gil into the woods a little way as they put some distance and then parralelled the trail, allowing them to both travel in their original direction and see the road in case more soldiers came along.

A few hours later the familiar beating of horse hooves sounded from the road and the two lowered themselves to avoid being seen. Gil and Nero watched as ten soldiers on horseback rode hard towards the village. “Where do you think they are off to?” Gil asked and Nero avoided shooting the annoyed look at the other man. “I have no earthly idea” he simply said as they both got up and continued walking.

“I would like to try and get a look at the village, we have not had any news recently and I want to see how things are progressing, the last time I went through a village, it was... not good” he said deciding to leave out the dead bodies and pillars of fire. Gil thought about it and then cautiously nodded “We will get close enough to try and see, but not too close, I don’t want to have to explain to the soldiers who we are and what we are doing, if my last attempt is any indication, everyone in this territory is now a slave and treated as such” he finished and Nero snapped up his head looking at the other man with a start.

“What do you mean?” he asked not having talked to a soldier or village save the dying man. Had things changed that much he thought waiting for Gil to speak. The old man looked off into the woods and then finally turned back to the Messenger. “I sat outside a village for a week looking on as they reorganized it, I heard the speeches and watched the people, the Empress has stripped the nobility of there land and titles and everyone works the fields. Even the houses and land of the commoners is no longer theres” he finished, and Nero could see the haunted look of resentment on his face. “That’s not all is it?” he asked, seeing the story on the man’s face and he shook his head. “There were those that resisted, protested, argued, they were slaughtered or hung from the walls as an example. Don’t kid yourself this brave new world of the Empress, its enslavement she is draining the kingdom dry for her wars” he finished, and Nero could hear the hate and bitterness in the man’s voice.

He couldn’t blame him he felt the same “The mages are involved” he whispered and Gil nodded “I have seen them, coming and taking control from the Seers, diplaying their power to show the commoners they are helpless, Aurtus damn them” he spit and then turned and started walking, his indication Nero thought that he was done talking.

A few hours later they spotted the walls of the small village and carefully made their way closer, trying to get a look inside. Angling for the entrance, which was open thankfully Nero thought they found a good spot to watch what was going on. Gil tapped Nero’s arm and pointed, the Messenger followed his finger and saw it, hanging on the wall was a woman, her black hair frosted with silver covered the naked breasts as her clothing had been removed and from the look of it, she had been beaten to death. “What village is this?” Gil asked shaking his head at the sight. “Its veripose” Nero said without emotion, still staring at the woman hanging from the wall. “How do you know?” Gil asked curiously and Nero pointed towards the woman. “That is messenger farrow histurn, she was a good caring woman, someone who cared about her flock” he said anger roiling at what they had done to someone who served Aurtus. “May you be accepted into the arms of Aurtus, may they sing of your deeds in the great feasting halls” he whispered, giving her the blessing of passing as a tear escaped his eye.

“The monsters” Gil spat, they continued to watch the village for several hours they witnessed the people coming out of the messenger hall, lining up and being led out of the village guarded as they made their way out towards the surrounding farms. They continued to watch and saw it when a boy, one carefully watching the guards, slipped into the brush when he wasn’t looking.

“Go, lets get him” Nero whispered pushing Gil urgently as they watched him slink through the brush and away from the line of commoners. The two moved silently as possible, though neither were Wardens and probably made enough noise to more then give themselves away, fortunately the young man was more concerned about watching towards the road and just about had a heart attack when Gil grabbed him from behind.

“Calm down, we are not going to hurt you” Nero breathed, the boy struggled until he finally saw the messenger robes that Nero wore. “You’re a messenger, like Messenger Histurn” he said, and Nero winced.

“I am, Messenger Histurn was a friend” he said gently, and the young man calmed down. Gil let him go and they moved further into the woods and out of sight of the village and the road. They settled next to an old fallen tree, the trunk large enough to hide the small group from any prying eyes.

“What is your name” Nero asked gently putting a hand on the young man to reassure him. “Kip, my name is Kip” he said, looking into his face Nero could see the relief and fear as the tears well up in his eyes the relief of being away from the soldiers evident. “Kip, what happened to Messenger Histurn?” he asked but Nero wasn’t sure he wanted to hear the answer. The young man winced as he thought back to the events that had led up to his friend and fellow Messenger hanging on the wall.

“When the soldiers came, they gathered everyone, told them they no longer owned anything, that they were to serve the Empress, that there homes and farms now belonged to the crown, Messenger Histurn stepped forward and argued saying this wouldn’t stand, that she would take it to the Empress and the Lord Reagent, but the soldiers just laughed, they beat her, stripped her.. did horrible things to her and then hung her from the wall telling everyone this is what happened when you did not follow the Empresss orders” he finished wincing as he saw the rage building on Nero’s face. “The Lord Seer came, he is a mage Messenger, he killed my parents with a wave of his hand, told everyone they were now property, we were forced to live in Aurtus’s keep and from there, brought out daily to work the farm, the soldiers never let us out of there sight” he said, Nero could hear the anger and bitterness in this young man. Whatever happened from here, this would stay with the child and it would define him he thought. “Kip, we are heading north, we are leaving the territory, you can come” Nero said but the boy shook his head. “I have family in Turen, I am going their Messenger, I will never return here again, I hope Turen attacks and kills the Black Empress” he spat.

Kip stayed for a meal, the three eating in silence and once done, Kip said his goodbyes, the three parting ways as Kip went west and the two men went north. Nero was roiling over the Empress’s use of the keeps as slave quarters, what right did she have “Blasphemer” he whispered to himself. The two following the road again from afar, they eventually caught up with the line of commoners as they made their way towards another farm. Nero noticed it was shorter, they must have dropped off the first crew he thought looking on with impudent rage as he watchd the faces of the people.

They were without hope he thought, and he said a small prayer, hoping someone would hear. He again said a small prayer for those who now found themselves under the boot of the Black Empress, “We need to move Messenger, we can’t stay here too long lest they discover us and if they do I fear our future will be the same as thiers” Gil whispered, he had been giving Nero worried glances since they had come upon the line of commoners again. “What is bothering you Gil, why do you look so worried?” Nero asked finally turning and reguarding the other man. Gil sighed shaking his head “it’s the look in your eyes Messenger, I have seen that before, if you are thinking of taking on that group of soldiers, you will either be hanging from a pole yourself or walking the line with the commoners” he said and Nero could see the worried look in the man’s eyes. He is worried about being left alone he thought nodding at the man “I have no intention of killing myself, but this cannot stand Gil, this cannot be the fate of this country, someone needs to do something” he said and the frustration from weeks of watching the territory descend into madness coming out as he spoke.

They left the area of the small village as they continued to make their way North, no more soldiers were seen that day as the rest of the walk until they settled down for the night had been uneventful. “I don’t understand what the Empress is doing Gil” Nero finally said as the two laid down, settling in for the night and the other man looked over the dark woods as he listened to the creatures calls as they echoed within the trees. “I don’t know, I am a businessman and from a money standpoint it doesn’t make much sense. The Emporer had fostered peace and the country had grown wealthy and happy, as soon as he dies the Empress begins to change things, to subjugate the people, strip the nobles, there is something we are missing, otherwise Messsenger its just madness, in which case the only solution would be to depose the woman before she causes permanent damage” he finished and Nero nodded taking his statement to heart.

Who would be able to take control of the country, she stripped the nobility, he was sure anyone who could be a challenge to the throne would have been killed, including the Lord Reagent, in times of strife there was a law allowing the church to take control until a proper ruler could be found and then he remembered the ring, pulling it out he studied it again, his order had fallen apart as well there was no Lord Reagent to take control to build an army and order troops to take the capital he thought looking down at the ring, finally with a forlorn sigh he put it away, feeling the weight of the gold object in his pocket.

Nero slept fitfully finally giving up about the time the sun began to rise over the group as the first light of morning peeked through the trees. He sat thinking about the ring and the Lord Reagent as well as the people of the territory and the looks of those poor farmers and workers. They had no hope, no one to rally them and no one to step in and solve the situation the country now found itself.

“How long have you been up?” came a raspy voice from behind him and he turned smiling to find Gil getting up and looking mussed as he shambled towards the treeline to relieve himself. “A while couldn’t sleep, he said turning back to give the man some semblance of privacy. The mornings were still cold despite the warm days they turned into and Nero pulled his robe tight as the chill attempted to sink into his bones. The two men had breakfast and discussed little as they saved their energy for the trip. “We are about two days out of the border, as long as its not guarded we should be able to get across easily” Gil said, Nero nodding not really knowing much about the border, though he had heard there were no troops that guarded the barrens, not for at least a decade. When the agreement was first signed, the entire border had troops along it, but since no one ever tried to go either to the barrens or from them, they eventually downsized the guard contingent and then disbanding it.

But that was before the Empress had changed everything, it was very possible there would be guards he thought putting away the smoked beef strips and taking a few gulps of water. After packing up the two men set out north again, but there mood was a little lighter, the distance from the village of the day before along with being close to there destination put both men in, if not a good mood, then a better one the cloud that had hung over them seemed to have dissipated Nero reflected as they shared stories and observations both men smiling.

Midday the two had come to a river forcing them to move up the bank until they found a bridge. Ensuring that no patrol would happen by the men quickly crossed and right into the trap the small group of bandits had set. As Nero came off the old bridge, men and women both appeared from around the trees, boxing in the two men. Nero did not see them until it was too late but once they had shown themselves the Messenger put himself in between his friend and the bandits.

The dress looked familiar and it took him only a moment to recognize the brand on the cheeks of the bandits “Mages” he said spitting the word. Why is it always mages he thought, the root of the problems over the past months had always seem to go back to Mages, this is not a coincidence he reflected, but dismissed the thought, right now they were in danger, the desperate look in the eyes of the group surrounding them told Nero that he should tread carefully. “At ease my friends, we have no valuables and are simply a couple of poor travelers looking to remove ourselves from the soldiers of Vicor” Nero said “I am a simple Messenger, one bound to help those who need it, how can we be of aid my children” he finished letting them know he was of the church and would do what he could for the group. Gil eyed the group trying to get a bearing on them.

They all looked hungry and dirty as if they had been traveling hard for the past few days. “Mior, it’s a Messenger, he could help” one of the younger mages said to the big one who stood out in front. “Shut up” he said raising his hand as if he was going to hit the younger one. He flinched, melding into the crowd as the others stood and watched. “Mior, your group looks hungry, we do not have a lot but are willing to share” Nero said, pulling the pack from his shoulder, but before he could open it, Mior reached over and snatched it. “Thank you, we will take all of it” he said and then nodded towards someone behind him and he could hear Gil curse as someone grabbed his pack too.” Nero turned and locked eyes with Gil, who was about to protest “Its fine, take it with our compliments” he said keeping eye contact with Gil, the man was boiling and Nero could see it, but if he went off, they were liable to get hurt.

“Now see, here is a man who knows that Mages are the superior being, meant to be served” Mior said turning to his group and smiling. There was nervous laughter, but not a lot of them Nero noticed. Nero bit back the scathing comment that tried to slip out., “You have what you want, we will leave now” he said trying to step around the small group but Mior was not done with them, his eyes looked unfocused and there was deep rage there Nero thought. “No, we aren’t quite done, you see, we need a few servants to carry our things and you two will do nicely” he said smiling back to his group. Nero closed his eyes and took a breath, but while he was doing that Gil had finally had enough.

“Bunch of stupid mage thugs, who think they are big and bad, if your so big and bad, why are you hiding like children in the woods, picking on a messenger of all things, you have no honor, spark” he finished, using the derogatory term most commoners used for Mages. Nero saw Mior as he turned to Gil, his eyes were dark, dangerous. He tried to step inbetween, tried to stop the man but before he knew what had happened, he felt pain in his stomach and looked down to find the end of a mage dagger buried to the hilt. “What” he said, not understanding as he fell to the ground. One of the mages reached out making a gesture with his hand and Gil was held still as two other mages stabbed him, over and over the look on his face was pain and anger as he finally dropped, blood coursing down his shirt. “what the hell did you do that for dammit” one man said turning to Mior, the leader turned and backhanded the other man “Because no one talks to me like that, we are the gifted not these dirtborn” he said kicking Nero as he lay there bleeding on the ground, he held his hand over the wound tighly despite the pain, doing his best to try and staunch the bleeding. He shifted his view and saw the others pull the daggers from Gils body.

Gil, who had never done anything to deserve this, had done nothing but help people, help him and now these mages had just killed him. “May Aurtus flay out alive and serve you to Mephis, may your soul be used as an outhouse” he whispered weezing through the pain. Mior laughed and shook his head “Messenger, feel free to tell him, after all you will see him first” he said and raised the dagger but as he took a step to drive it into Nero’s head, someone grabbed his arm “Soldiers” he whispered and the leaders eyes went wide as Nero lay forgotten on the ground. “Go, go” he said, and the mages melded into the forest.

Nero felt himself fading and knew he didn’t have a lot of time before the soldiers found him. Rolling as best he could the messenger rolled off the trail and into the brush, trying to put distance between him and the patrol that even now was coming to the bridge. He reached over and brushed dirt over the trail of blood doing his best to hide it, he didn’t need the soldiers following the trail he thought wincing at the pain the motion of his arm caused.

He listened as boots made a hollow sound on the wood of the bridge and finaly he could hear voices as the small patrol approached. “Any sign of the mages, there have been reports they frequent this area, more then one of our soldiers have been jumped for supplies” said one. There was silence and then someone answered. “Sir, blood and footprints, take a look” Nero closed his eyes saying a small prayer they weren’t trackers. After a few moments the first voice returned. “The book tracks go this way, spread out and be wary” he said, and Nero heard the sound of metal on leather as the weapons were unsheathed.

He lay there for what seemed like an eternity but mercifully no soldier stumbled upon him, finally he heard one of them call out, but they were much further up the path. He breathed a sigh of relief, but the relief was short lived, his hand was soaked with his own blood and he felt lightheaded, he had lost a lot of blood he thought. Nero quickly took the braided rope that held his messenger robes closed, pulling out a small knife from his belt, he did his best to clumsily cut a section of the heavy robe while trying to hold the wound. Using the rope and the large piece of cloth folded a few times, he covered the wound, pulling the blade with a hiss as he did his best to hold his tongue, knowing that any screams would bring the soldiers back. Once the blade was removed blood flowed freely and he quickly covered it with the cloth, cinching the rope as tight as he could, tears coming to his eyes as his stomach burned from the tightness of the rope. But the blood slowed and though the piece of cloth was saturated, it was sticky and drying.

Nero couldn’t feel any new blood, he was still lightheaded and without medical care, he would die he thought. His resolve hardening to steel as he rose unsteadily to his feet, using trees he pushed himself north. He didn’t make it far before the loss of blood caused him to collapse, laying there he looked up at the trees staring up towards the light of day. He was going to die here he thought his vision slowly going to black.

Then an odd thing as his vision darkened, he looked up to see people jumping tree to tree high above, he was having hallucinations he thought as he finally went unconscious.
